description: FEAT-2326609747 (services.convergence) inc1 canonical action list -- v2, independent round r1 remediation. The SAME entries drive BOTH sides of the services/wellbeing-coverage parity fixture: webconsole/test/converge-fixture-emit-services.mjs (TS data.ts serviceCoverageOf, via a directly-authored, already-online building set, using each entry's tsSpec) and internal/converge/services_domain.go's ServicesDomain (Go engine.services ServicesAPI, driven directly per AC-8 of docs/planning/acceptance/FEAT-services-convergence-inc1-2026-09-02.md). Shape mirrors internal/converge/domain.go's Journal/JournalEntry ({tick, op, args}), reusing the SAME codeJournalOpFailed (MET-H503) failure code.
r1RemediationNote: v1 seeded Go capacity with a hand-authored 'goCapacity' literal chosen to numerically match the TS building's capacity -- the independent round REJECTed this: it concealed that engine.services' own coverageRatio() clamps to [0,1] while TS's serviceCoverageOf does not (a coverageRatio()*0.5 mutation left the whole suite green), and that the Go and TS catalogues use genuinely different capacity UNITS for the same building kind (Go's fire_station is '4 appliances', TS's fire_post is 'served=4000 people'). v2 replaces 'goCapacity' with 'buildingID', a REAL data/buildings.json catalogue id -- services_domain.go now sources capacity via services.ServiceSpecFromBuilding (the same route internal/engine/build/build.go's registerServiceLocked uses), so a scratch-edit to that catalogue entry's capacityRaw is visible to a fresh run, and the Go-vs-TS capacity divergence this now surfaces is an HONEST finding (docs/planning/acceptance/FEAT-services-convergence-inc1-2026-09-02.md's Addendum), not something this fixture papers over.
goBuildingIDs: Only 8 data/buildings.json entries currently carry the serviceKind/coverageRadius/staffingNeed fields registerServiceLocked's bridge requires (grep -n '"serviceKind"' data/buildings.json): clinic/small_hospital/general_hospital/teaching_hospital (healthcare), one_room_school/primary_school/secondary_school (education), fire_station (fire). This journal uses fire_station (buildingID='fire_station', capacityRaw='4 appliances'), primary_school (capacityRaw='240'), and clinic (capacityRaw='150 visits/d') -- one Go building per compared group. Police/power have NO serviceKind-tagged catalogue entry today (confirmed by the same grep), so they are NOT compared rows in this increment -- see the acceptance doc's Addendum correcting the original mapping table's 'police is 1:1-ready' framing.
placementNote: place_service on the TS side appends the building directly to state.buildings with builtTick:null (isOnline()'s own 'always online' branch, data.ts:461) instead of routing through the reducer's 'place' case -- this scenario tests serviceCoverageOf's capacity/demand arithmetic, not gameplay realism. tsSpec drives the TS side; buildingID+goKind+goServiceID drive the Go side (services_domain.go) -- two independent catalogues read from the SAME journal entry, which is the whole point of AC-3's 'same logical input' requirement now that the two sides no longer share a hand-picked number.
populationNote: set_population assigns state.population (TS) / the journal-local population variable ServicesDomain.Run tracks (Go) directly, exactly as place_service bypasses gameplay.

entries.note: Checkpoint 1: TS is comfortably over-provisioned for every group (its buildings are sized for thousands); Go's real catalogue capacities (4 appliances / 240 pupils / 150 visits per day) are already tiny relative to a population of 100 -- fire and healthcare are already under 1.0 engine coverage here, education is not (240 pupils vs a 23-child need).
Checkpoint 2: every Go group now reads well under 1.0 engine coverage; TS remains comfortably covered at this population for every group except fire (2000/4000=0.5).

Checkpoint 3: TS itself now reads under 1.0 for every compared group (fire 4000/12000=0.333, education 1830/2760=0.663, healthcare 5000/24000=0.208), and Go's real catalogue capacities are further under-provisioned still (4/12000, 240/2760, 150/24000) -- the checkpoint the demand-push-load-bearing self-consistency tests (services_domain_test.go) pin their expected engine values against, since demand genuinely binds capacity for every group here.
